text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- National Electoral Council General Secretary Vu Mao has said that ensuring democracy, openess and justice will be the major tasks of the new National Assembly legislature.
-- Vietnam will carry out major research to assess the overall effects of toxic chemicals used by U.S. forces during the war.
-- Ho Chi Minh City's party chief has said more advantage should be given to foreign investors including readjustment of land rentals, improvement in power supply and simplification of procedures.
-- Vietnam has so far included 1,496 groups of imported items in a list of goods subject to the Common Effective Preferential Tarriffs scheme.
-- Vietnam's General Rubber Corporation has reported output of 49,295 tonnes of rubber in the first half of 1997, up by 8.1 percent compared with the same period last year.
-- Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi has said Vietnam attaches importance to the traditional consolidation and strengthening of friendship and multi-faced cooperation with Poland.
-- Hanoi's municipal authorities have issued instructions on efforts to reinforce the capital's dyke system as the flooding season is expected to arrive shortly.
